identity.title: Spatially Resolved [C II] Emission in SPT0346-52: A Hyper-starburst Galaxy Merger at z ∼ 5.7

paper_type_evidence.quote: we present $\sim 0.15\ensuremath{''}$ ALMA observations of the \[CII\]158$\rm{\mu m}$ emission line in this $z = 5.7$ dusty star-forming galaxy.

evidence.quote: SPT0346-52 is a gravitationally lensed galaxy at $z=5.6559$ (cite: weiss2013), with lensing magnification $\mu = 5.6\pm 0.1$ (cite: spilker2016).

evidence.quote: We discuss the \[CII\] deficit with a pixellated study of the $\rm{L_{[C{\scriptsize II}]}/L_{FIR}}$ ratio in the source plane.

method.value: Pixellated visibility-plane reconstruction with SIE (z=0.9) plus external shear; lens parameters from MCMC, regularization lambda iterated

evidence.quote: We model the lensing galaxy as a singular isothermal ellipsoid at $z=0.9$ with an external shear component.

key_parameters.value: lambda fitted for fixed lens model, alternating with MCMC until convergence

evidence.quote: We fit for $\lambda$, then run the MCMC with RIPPLES. These two steps are repeated until the chains have converged
singular isothermal ellipsoid at $z=0.9$

evidence.quote: The model visibilities are compared to the observed visibilities via a $\chi^2$ goodness-of-fit test.

validation.value: Mock point-source visibilities reconstructed to give effective source-plane resolution

evidence.quote: we created a set of mock visibilities for a point source in the source plane that was lensed by the best-fit lens model.

findings_qualitative.value: Two spatially/kinematically separated components joined by a gas bridge; dust continuum is more compact and smoother than [CII].

evidence.quote: The lensing reconstruction reveals two spatially and kinematically separated components

claims.hypothesis: Does the [CII] deficit hold at sub-kpc scales?
claims.experiment: Pixel-by-pixel L_CII/L_FIR vs Sigma_FIR in source plane

evidence.quote: individual pixels within the galaxy follow the same trend found using unresolved observations of other galaxies

claims.hypothesis: Is SPT0346-52 a merger or a rotating disk?
claims.result: Two components ~1 kpc and ~500 km/s apart with bridge
claims.finding: Major merger likely driving star formation

evidence.quote: We argue that SPT0346-52 is undergoing a major merger
Both components are found to be globally unstable, with Toomre Q instability parameters $\ll 1$ everywhere.

why_this_method.value: Pixellated source does not assume a specific source structure and uses all interferometric data

evidence.quote: it does not assume a specific source structure

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Clumpy rotating disk considered; merger favored given higher S/N

evidence.quote: allowing a more confident classification of this system as a merger rather than a clumpy, rotating disk.

limitations_admitted.value: Constant dust temperature assumed, uncertainty within factor ~2

evidence.quote: the variation caused by variable dust temperatures in the galaxy is within a factor of $\sim 2$.
